releases.name: v0.15.0 — OpenCode 2 deliveries steer by default
releases.body:
## OpenCode 2 deliveries steer by default

A message now reaches a model that is mid-turn, instead of waiting for the turn to end and arriving when the facts in it may already be stale.

**Measured on a live v2, not assumed:** two deliveries landed in the middle of a 40-file task, at steps 5 and 17, and one message survived cancelling the turn. One delivery was accepted and never read because it arrived on the recipient's last tool call and the turn ended first — a delivery racing the end of a turn, not a lost message.

Switching back is one setting, no rebuild:

- `"v2Delivery": "queue"` in the plugin options
- or AGENTPOST_V2_DELIVERY=queue in the environment

OpenCode 1 has no such choice and is unaffected.

### Removed in the same change

An earlier idea announced unread mail from the context hook before each model dispatch. It could not work: delivery already hands the message to session.prompt and deletes it from the inbox, so by the next dispatch there was nothing left to announce. A unit test against a fake context could not show that — a live v2 did, in one run.

### Upgrade note

ccepted on OpenCode 2 now means OpenCode admitted the message for that session, not that it sat in a durable queue. `^0.14.1` will not pick this up automatically; `^0.15.0` will.

- **A registration failure now says why.** `send` re-attempts `autoRegister` and, when that fails, answers `E_NOT_REGISTERED` with the reason and what to do about it, instead of letting a raw filesystem error escape. It matters because the hooks that register a session log the failure at a level that is off by default, and `agentpost_peers`, `agentpost_fetch` and `agentpost_deliveries` do not require registration: a session that could not register could browse the mesh indefinitely without learning it was not on it.
- **npm publishing moved into the release** through trusted publishing: no `NPM_TOKEN` in the repository, `--provenance` on the tarball, and the tag and `package.json` must agree before anything is published. Triggered by publishing a release, not by a push to `main`.
- **The rejected-by-design reasoning moves into `AGENTS.md`** and the stale Phase 4 backlog file is gone. The file-lease and metrics rejections are worth keeping precisely because they were expensive to reach: the lease keying trap is the same one that already cost us the address.
- **Two claims in `AGENTS.md` corrected** that had drifted from the code: it said no CI existed, and that inheritance carried `description`/`metadata` along with the address — which 0.14.0 removed, because a copied description is a lie that peers read as fact.

Upgrade: `opencode` picks the new version automatically if you pin `@vdrsl/opencode-agentpost`. No configuration change.

releases.name: v0.14.0 — one package for OpenCode 1 and 2
releases.body:
- **The same package now runs on OpenCode 2.** The default export carries both entrypoints: V1 reads `server()` and V2 reads `setup()`, which is the dual form OpenCode documents. That needs 1.18.29 or newer on the V1 side — the first release accepting an object entrypoint, and older than any release this package was published to. Install under `plugin` on V1 and `plugins` on V2; nothing else differs.
- **V2 delivery uses the runtime's queue.** V1 discovered a busy recipient through `session.status` and deferred the message itself, up to `maxBusyDefers`. V2 removed that API and made the choice part of the request, so delivery is one call with `delivery: "queue"`. This plugin never asks whether a session is busy under V2: a second queue built on the first is how messages get lost twice.
- **`accepted` under V2 means "admitted to that session's durable queue"** — the promise resolving with the admitted inbox item. It never meant the model read the message, and under V2 it does not even mean the session went idle. The other four states are unchanged.
- Tool descriptions moved to `src/descriptions.ts`, shared by both runtimes. The model reads them as instructions, so a V1 build and a V2 build describing the same tool differently would be two projects wearing one name with nothing failing.
- Under V2 a session's own activity marker is no longer refreshed by mail another agent injects into it: V2 does not run the prompt hook for synthetic messages. `idleMs` still tracks the human's own turns, which is what it claims to measure.
- **Fix, found on a real v2.0.22: every V2 tool call failed** with "Tool result declared output without an output schema". The plugin registered cleanly and then each call failed, so nothing behind a fake context ever saw it. `Tool.Info` carries `output?: JsonSchema` and the result must match it; all five tools return pretty-printed JSON text, so one schema now covers them and the test asserts it.

releases.name: v0.7.0: reap orphan inboxes, activity markers and processed markers
releases.body:
## Cleanup

Storage stops growing: an agent that is gone for good no longer leaves a trail of
empty inbox directories, activity markers and replay markers behind.

### Fixed

- `Registry.unregister()` removes `activity/<id>` next to the record, so an agent
  deletes its own activity marker and the record reaper takes it along. The marker
  is owner state, so nobody else may touch it.
- `queueRetentionMs` (default 5 min, `AGENTMESH_QUEUE_RETENTION_MS`) and
  `Registry.cleanupOrphanedInboxes()`: an inbox directory is dropped only when all
  three hold — the agent has no record, the inbox is empty, and it has been untouched
  for that long. A peer that just unregistered keeps its queue, so a message sent
  moments before is still there when it comes back.
- `processedRetentionMs` (default 24 h, `AGENTMESH_PROCESSED_RETENTION_MS`) and
  `Registry.cleanupProcessed()`: replay-suppression markers age out by mtime instead
  of accumulating forever. After the window a duplicate delivery is possible again;
  keep it above your longest plausible delivery gap.
- All of it runs in the existing one-per-minute sweep, so no new timer and no new
  ownership. `unregisterSession()` still deletes nothing: an id can be re-registered
  by the next session in that directory, and a non-empty inbox is undelivered work.
- New log events `orphans_cleaned` and `processed_cleaned`, carrying a `count`.

### Compatibility

Two new options, both defaulted and additive. Nothing on disk is removed that the
old code would have kept. Tests: 119 (was 109), new `test/cleanup.test.ts`.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/Vdrsl/opencode-agentmesh-private/compare/v0.6.0...v0.7.0

releases.name: v0.6.0: peer freshness and non-dropping busy delivery
releases.body:
## Peer freshness and non-dropping busy delivery

### Added

- `PeerView.idleMs` — milliseconds since a peer's last session turn, read from a new
  owner-owned `<home>/activity/<id>` file that is `touch`ed on every `chat.message` and
  `session.idle`. Agents registered before this release fall back to the record mtime.
- `agentmesh_peers` reports `idleMs` and lists peers **freshest first**: alive before
  stale, then least idle, id as the tie-break. A chat nobody opened for two days now
  looks different from the session someone is actually working in, without adding an
  `idle` status or hiding anyone.
- A model rule in the injected prompt: pick the peer with the smallest `idleMs`, and if
  every candidate has been idle for hours, say so instead of dropping a question into a
  dead chat.

### Fixed

- A message is no longer deleted when a peer's session stays busy past `maxBusyDefers`.
  The recipient now writes an `ambiguous` ack and returns the claim to its inbox with the
  defer count, so the message is injected as soon as that session goes idle.
  `busyDeferMs` drops from `5000` to `2000` — a busy peer is a slow peer, not a lost one.
- `agentmesh_send` guidance: a busy peer reporting `queued` is normal. Do not resend.
- Windows: inbox assertions ignore the `.tmp` scratch an atomic write can leave behind,
  and temp-home cleanup retries on `ENOTEMPTY` (the crash-matrix C1 flake).

### Compatibility

No breaking changes. The activity file is additive — a peer that does not write one is
measured from its record mtime. `AGENTMESH_BUSY_DEFER_MS` still overrides the new default.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/Vdrsl/opencode-agentmesh-private/compare/bdbc8bf...v0.6.0
